purpose: Measure whether one source-grounded Class C edit adds material presentation utility over the already reviewed deterministic A/B candidate without increasing product-identity risk enough to negate the gain.

reviewedReference.deterministicCandidate: whole factual two-piece group aligned horizontally after connected-light-neutral background isolation

allowed: cleaner subject/background boundary than the nearest-neighbor deterministic research render
more natural antialiasing/resampling while preserving the same factual group
neutral white canvas completion that does not invent product pixels or scene context
minor presentation cleanup that is visible at the target placement size
notAnObjective: changing the product to fill more area than the reviewed A/B geometry permits
creating a prettier but less source-faithful replacement

fidelityInvariants: exactly two primary slide pieces remain visible
preserve characteristic rail proportions and relative lengths
preserve visible holes, slots, fittings and terminal structures
no duplicated, removed or invented hardware
no new labels, logos or markings
semantic orientation remains horizontal for the wide placement
source identity/authority remains attached to the result

evaluation.successRule: Class C is justified only if it produces a clearly visible presentation-quality improvement over the reviewed A/B candidate while passing the same fidelity review with no new unresolved product-detail questions.

stopConditions: any changed or invented hole/fitting/rail geometry
any unsupported product reconstruction required to make the result look cleaner
the gain is merely cosmetic at magnified inspection but not visible in the 440x180 placement
human review cannot confidently distinguish presentation cleanup from factual reconstruction

integrationBoundary.doNotUseSoftExtraSoftCloseOrPistonForFir: Their source-authority caveats would confound the first generation-risk comparison.
